country3-usage.title: Countries and directions
country3-usage.body: English uses which for all three; Swedish agrees with the noun.

perfect3-usage.title: Past, perfect and clause order
perfect3-usage.body: Swedish uses har with all perfect verbs here, including motion verbs. Main clauses put the finite verb second.

sources.title: Swedish grammar: clause structure and inflection

people3-usage.title: People and reasons
people3-usage.body: Swedish distinguishes Hur ser hon ut? (appearance) from Hur är hon? (character).

modals3-usage.title: Plans, calls and instructions
modals3-usage.body: Unlike English must, Swedish måste also works with personal subjects without changing form.

sources.title: Swedish grammar: clause structure and inflection

employment3-usage.title: Work and applications
employment3-usage.body: Som can be a relative word (who/that) or mean as in arbetar som lärare.

environment3-usage.title: Environment and comparison
environment3-usage.body: Unlike English than, än introduces the comparison in both regular and irregular forms.

sources.title: Swedish grammar: clause structure and inflection

renting3-usage.title: Renting and housing
renting3-usage.body: Ingen/inget/inga combines no with noun agreement. Distinguish an indefinite and a definite plural.

traffic3-usage.title: Traffic and journeys
traffic3-usage.body: Short answers repeat the auxiliary, much as English does: Har du …? Ja, det har jag.

budget3-usage.title: Bills and a budget
budget3-usage.body: Låna has the direction borrow; the particle ut changes it to lend.

clinic3-usage.title: At the clinic
clinic3-usage.body: English too becomes också in positive statements; not … either becomes inte … heller.

relationships3-usage.title: Relationships and messages
relationships3-usage.body: Swedish usually retains att where English can omit that. Vilken/vilket/vilka in exclamations agrees with the noun.

society3-usage.title: Politics and public services
society3-usage.body: Varken … eller already expresses neither … nor; do not add inte to make that meaning.
